Bug_Title: RV: Bad attempt to compute absolute value of signed 32-bit hashcode (RV_ABSOLUTE_VALUE_OF_HASHCODE)
Bug_Details:
This code generates a hashcode and then computes
the absolute value of that hashcode.  If the hashcode
is Integer.MIN_VALUE, then the result will be negative as well (since
Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE).
 One out of 2^32 strings have a hashCode of Integer.MIN_VALUE,
including "polygenelubricants" "GydZG_" and ""DESIGNING WORKHOUSES".
 Integer.MIN_VALUE Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by attempting to compute the absolute value of a hashcode using Math.abs(). Specifically, if the input string's hashcode is Integer.MIN_VALUE, Math.abs() will return Integer.MIN_VALUE, which is incorrect since the absolute value should be positive.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with specific strings that have a hashcode of Integer.MIN_VALUE. The expected result is Integer.MAX_VALUE, but due to the bug, the actual result is Integer.MIN_VALUE, causing the test to fail.
